!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = AutoCUT&Tag_Protocols_io.pdf
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = CUT&Tag uses tagmentation in which the barcoded adapters are integrated on both sides of the insert, so that the DNA that is released is already a barcoded library. PMID:31036827
!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for H3K4me1 in sorted CD45+ cells from the AML-1 patient sample
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cut&tag antibody: ELL Cell Signaling Technologies cat# 14468S
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = cell type: sorted CD45+ cells from the AML-2 KMT2A-ENL patient sample
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = genomic DNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = AutoCUT&Tag_Protocols_io.pdf
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = CUT&Tag uses tagmentation in which the barcoded adapters are integrated on both sides of the insert, so that the DNA that is released is already a barcoded library. PMID:31036827
!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for ELL in sorted CD45+ cells from the AML-2 patient sample
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = CUT&Tag uses tagmentation in which the barcoded adapters are integrated on both sides of the insert, so that the DNA that is released is already a barcoded library. PMID:31036827
!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for H3K27me3 in sorted CD45+ cells from the MPAL-1 patient sample
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for H3K9me3 in sorted CD45+ cells from the MPAL-2 patient sample

!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = CUT&Tag uses tagmentation in which the barcoded adapters are integrated on both sides of the insert, so that the DNA that is released is already a barcoded library. PMID:31036827
!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for H3K9me3 in the RS4;11 KMT2Ar cell line
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = AutoCUTnTag_protocols_io.pdf
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = CUT&Tag uses tagmentation in which the barcoded adapters are integrated on both sides of the insert, so that the DNA that is released is already a barcoded library. PMID:31036827
!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for Dot1L in sorted CD45+ cells from the AML-3 patient sample
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for H3K36me3 in sorted CD45+ cells from the AML-5 patient sample
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = CUT&Tag uses tagmentation in which the barcoded adapters are integrated on both sides of the insert, so that the DNA that is released is already a barcoded library. PMID:31036827
!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for H3K9me3 in sorted CD45+ cells from the AML-5 patient sample
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_description = Automated CUT&RUN for IgG control in the K562 myelogenous leukemia cell line
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = CUT&Tag uses tagmentation in which the barcoded adapters are integrated on both sides of the insert, so that the DNA that is released is already a barcoded library. PMID:31036827
!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for H3K27ac in sorted CD45+ cells from the MPAL-2 patient sample
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = CUT&Tag uses tagmentation in which the barcoded adapters are integrated on both sides of the insert, so that the DNA that is released is already a barcoded library. PMID:31036827
!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for H3K4me3 in the RS4;11 KMT2Ar cell line treated with 30 uM VTP50469 for 72hrs
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for H4K16ac in the SEM KMT2Ar cell line
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).

!Sample_description = Automated CUT&Tag for RNAP2S5p in the SEM KMT2Ar cell line grown with DMSO for 72hrs
!Sample_data_processing = Genome_build: UCSC hg19
!Sample_data_processing = 1. We used Bowtie2 2.4.1 with options "--end-to-end --very-sensitive --no-mixed --no-discordant -q --phred33 -I 10 -X 700" to map the paired-end 25bp reads to hg19 of Homo sapiens genomic sequence obtained from UCSC. 2. We extracted properly paired reads from Homo sapiens alignments to generate a bed files <chr> <start> <stop> <length> <strand> (Supplementary file hg19_fragments.bed.gz).  3. We used bedtools genomecov to make normalized count bedgraph files, which are the fraction of counts at each base pair scaled by the size of the reference sequence (3095693983) so that if the scaled counts were uniformly distributed there would be 1 at each position (Supplementary file normalized_counts.bedgraph.gz).
